prompt: Which access tier makes a blob unreadable until it is brought back?
hint: Three of the four answer in milliseconds.

choices.text: Cold
choices.why: Cold answers in milliseconds; what it changes is the price of reading.

choices.text: Cool
choices.why: Cool answers in milliseconds too.

choices.text: Archive
choices.why: Right. It has to be rehydrated first.

choices.text: Hot
choices.why: Hot is the tier with nothing extra to read.

prompt: Match each tier to its documented minimum days billed.
hint: They grow with how cold the tier is.

prompt: Where is a blob's access tier set?
hint: One container held three tiers side by side.

choices.text: On each block blob, with the account's default for blobs given none
choices.why: Right. Blobs with no tier of their own report the default as inferred.

choices.text: On the container, and every blob in it shares it
choices.why: Containers have no tier; the lesson set two different tiers in one.

choices.text: On the account only, so moving data between tiers means moving accounts
choices.why: That describes performance, Standard or Premium, not access tiers.

choices.text: On every blob type alike: block, append and page
choices.why: An append blob was refused with `AccessTierNotSupportedForBlobType`.

prompt: Moving ten million 4 KB log blobs from hot to cool saves almost nothing on storage, and the bill for the month goes up. Why?
hint: What is billed per blob rather than per gigabyte?

choices.text: Cool charges more per gigabyte kept than hot for small blobs
choices.why: The price per gigabyte kept is lower in cool whatever the blob's size.

choices.text: Cool keeps an extra copy of each blob, doubling the storage
choices.why: Copies are decided by the account's replication, not by the tier.

choices.text: The blobs were rehydrated first, at the high priority price
choices.why: Rehydration is for leaving archive; nothing here was archived.

choices.text: Ten million tier changes, each an operation at cool's price
choices.why: Right. The data is about 40 GB; the operations are ten million.

prompt: A blob was uploaded without `--tier`. `az storage blob show` reports `Hot` and `blobTierInferred: true`. What does that mean?
hint: Who chose the tier?

choices.text: Azure watched how the blob is used and moved it to hot
choices.why: Nothing watched anything; the blob was just uploaded.

choices.text: It follows the account's default
choices.why: Right. A tier set on the blob would say `false` and stay put.

choices.text: The tier was set on the blob and cannot be changed again
choices.why: `set-tier` changed the same blob to cold a moment later.

choices.text: Azurite could not read the tier and guessed
choices.why: Azure reports the same flag for the same reason.

prompt: Why does the Terraform provider refuse `access_tier = "Archive"` on a storage account?
hint: What would happen to every blob uploaded without a tier?

choices.text: Archive is not offered in `brazilsouth`
choices.why: validate checks the value against a list and knows nothing about regions.

choices.text: Archive is set blob by blob, never by default
choices.why: Right. The accepted list was `Cold`, `Cool`, `Hot`, `Premium` and `Smart`.

choices.text: The value is spelt `ARCHIVE` in capitals
choices.why: The list printed mixed case, `Cold` and `Cool`, and had no archive in any case.

choices.text: Terraform needs the account to be created before a tier is set
choices.why: `Cool` validated in the same file a moment earlier.

prompt: Quitanda moves a 2 TB folder of photos from cool back to hot, the week after moving it to cool. What does Microsoft document that the move is billed as?
hint: Warming a blob reads it out of the tier it leaves, and the week matters.

choices.text: Nothing: tier changes are free and only storage is billed
choices.why: Each change is an operation, and warming adds a price per gigabyte.

choices.text: A write in hot for each blob, and nothing more
choices.why: That is how cooling is billed, in the destination tier.

choices.text: A full rehydration, at standard priority
choices.why: Rehydration applies only to archive.

choices.text: Cool reads and retrieval, plus early deletion
choices.why: Right. A week is short of cool's 30 days.

prompt: Downloading a blob in the archive tier is refused with the error code ___.
hint: Two words, run together.

prompt: On Azure, a rehydration of a 2 GB blob to hot at standard priority has just started. What does a download return for the next few hours?
hint: Azurite finished at once; Azure does not.

choices.text: `BlobArchived`, until the rehydration finishes
choices.why: Right. The tier keeps saying `Archive` and the status says `rehydrate-pending-to-hot`.

choices.text: The content, slowly, as the blob comes back
choices.why: There is no partial read; the blob stays offline until the end.

choices.text: The content, at once, as Azurite showed
choices.why: That is the emulator's shortcut, not Azure's behaviour.

choices.text: `BlobNotFound`, because the blob is moved during rehydration
choices.why: The blob stays listed with its properties the whole time.

prompt: At standard priority, within how many hours does Microsoft document that an archived blob is rehydrated?
hint: The table in the section.

prompt: An auditor needs September's archived export this afternoon, and the archive copy must stay where it is. What does Quitanda do?
hint: Two ways out of archive, and two constraints.

choices.text: Change the archived blob's tier to hot at high priority
choices.why: Fast, but it moves the archive copy, which had to stay.

choices.text: Copy it to a new name at standard priority, which is cheaper and just as quick
choices.why: Standard is documented at up to 15 hours, too slow for this afternoon.

choices.text: Copy it to a new name in hot at high priority, leaving the archive copy
choices.why: Right. `rehydrate.py` did this; on Azure the copy is pending until the rehydration behind it ends.

choices.text: Download it directly; archive only delays the first byte
choices.why: A download of an archived blob is refused outright.

prompt: Why does Quitanda's archive account use LRS rather than the ZRS of its exports account?
hint: A tier and a replication option that do not go together.

choices.text: LRS is faster to rehydrate from
choices.why: Rehydration time depends on the priority, not on replication.

choices.text: Azurite only accepts archive on LRS
choices.why: Azurite has no replication and accepted every tier.

choices.text: Archived data is never worth three copies
choices.why: LRS also keeps three copies, in one datacentre.

choices.text: Archive is not offered on ZRS accounts at all
choices.why: Right, nor on GZRS or RA-GZRS, according to the documentation at the time of writing.

prompt: At an illustrative 0.010 USD per GB-month, what is one GB billed if it is moved to cool and deleted after 12 days? A month counts as 30 days.
hint: The minimum is billed in full.

prompt: What happens when a blob in cold is deleted on its twentieth day?
hint: Does anything stop the deletion?

choices.text: The deletion is refused until the 90 days have passed
choices.why: Nothing refuses it; Azurite and Azure both delete at once.

choices.text: It is moved to archive instead, to finish its minimum there
choices.why: No tier change happens on a delete.

choices.text: It is deleted, and 70 more days of cold are billed
choices.why: Right. The minimum arrives on the bill, not as a refusal.

choices.text: It is deleted, and the twenty days are refunded
choices.why: The days used are billed normally; it is the unused ones that are added.

prompt: A life-cycle rule archives blobs at 30 days and deletes them at 90. What does every blob it touches cost?
hint: How long does the blob stay in archive, and what is archive's minimum?

choices.text: 60 days of archive, the time it spent there
choices.why: Archive's minimum is 180 days and it is billed in full.

choices.text: 180 days of archive, though it stayed 60
choices.why: Right. 120 days of early deletion on every blob.

choices.text: Nothing extra, because a rule is exempt from early deletion
choices.why: The charge is about the blob's stay, whoever moves or deletes it.

choices.text: 90 days of cold, since the rule skips cool
choices.why: The rule moves to archive, not to cold.

prompt: With `year.py`'s illustrative prices, cool costs 122.88 a year and 10.24 per full read; hot costs 245.76 and nothing to read. How many full reads a year make the two cost the same?
hint: Divide the difference in the year by the price of a read.

prompt: In `year.py`'s last column, why is ten days in archive dearer than ten days in hot?
hint: How many days is each one billed for?

choices.text: Archive is billed for 180 days, and that outweighs its lower price
choices.why: Right. 12.29 against hot's 6.83.

choices.text: Archive's price per gigabyte is higher than hot's
choices.why: It is ten times lower in the program.

choices.text: The column includes a rehydration of the whole terabyte at the end of the ten days
choices.why: It keeps the data ten days and deletes it, with no read.

choices.text: Hot gives the first ten days for free
choices.why: Hot bills the ten days at its price: 6.83.

prompt: Quitanda's analysts reread one 500 GB table about twice a month. Using the arithmetic of `year.py`, which tier fits it?
hint: Twenty-four full reads a year; where is cool's break-even?

choices.text: Cold, because it is the cheapest online tier
choices.why: Cold's reads are the dearest online; 24 of them would cost far more than hot.

choices.text: Archive, because the table is large
choices.why: Size is not the question; a twice-monthly read cannot wait for a rehydration.

choices.text: Hot
choices.why: Right. At 24 reads a year, every cooler tier costs more.

choices.text: Cool, because it costs half as much to keep
choices.why: Its break-even with hot is 12 full reads a year; 24 is past it.

prompt: Order the tiers from the lowest price for keeping a gigabyte to the highest.
hint: The colder, the cheaper to keep.

prompt: Which of these did Azurite do that Azure would not? Choose all that apply.
hint: Look for the places where time or money would have shown.

choices.text: Finish a rehydration before the next command
choices.why: Yes; Azure documents up to 15 hours at standard priority.

choices.text: Delete a blob in cold after minutes, with no charge
choices.why: Yes; Azure would bill the rest of the 90 days.

choices.text: Refuse a download from archive with `BlobArchived`
choices.why: Azure refuses the same way.

choices.text: Refuse a tier on an append blob
choices.why: Azure refuses that too.

prompt: Which command moves an existing blob to the cold tier?
hint: One request, nothing copied.

choices.text: `az storage blob set-tier --tier Cold`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `az storage blob copy start --tier Cold`
choices.why: That makes a second blob under another name.

choices.text: `az storage blob upload --tier Cold --overwrite`
choices.why: That sends the content again to replace the blob.

choices.text: `az storage blob update --tier Cold`
choices.why: `update` changes content settings, not the tier.
